caption:
Build a date picker in your machine coding round with this line and every booking lands a month late.

Look at the card. The string "2026-12-05" gives you 12 for December. But the Date constructor counts months from 0: January is 0, December is 11. So month 12 means "one past December", and JavaScript quietly rolls it over to January of the next year. No error.

Fix: subtract 1 when you build the date, and add 1 when you show getMonth() to a person.

The year and the day of the month start where you'd expect. Only the month index starts at 0.

Source: MDN, Date() constructor (monthIndex).
